entries.310a3b9eb60614a9: It is an HDAC inhibitor for which an exclusive license was in-licensed from Astellas Pharma Inc. Because dose-limiting toxicity occurred in clinical trials in the United States, development in the cancer field has been suspended, and application in the ophthalmology field is currently being explored.
entries.33355b7257819a33: Originally developed as a treatment for HIV infection, it is a development-stage product expected to have applications in neurodegenerative diseases as a LINE-1 inhibitor. In June 2020 it granted an exclusive license with the right to sublicense worldwide to Transposon Therapeutics, Inc. of the United States, and future development is proceeding with it bearing all costs. Revenue of ¥28 million for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was entirely licensing income from that company.
entries.3b465694343cef67: This is the single segment of the Drug Discovery Business. It conducts research and development of drug candidates such as oncolytic viruses and antiviral therapeutics, and aims to commercialize them through licensing to pharmaceutical companies or through its own sales. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥28 million, all of which was income from licensees.
entries.43eb8fcc76f752b0: It is a next-generation oncolytic virus carrying the tumor suppressor gene p53. It is being developed for various solid cancers such as pancreatic cancer and is at the non-clinical stage. Manufacturing is planned to be outsourced to other manufacturing companies.
entries.5d09f0d2043cafb1: It is a genetically modified virus that specifically emits fluorescence in cells with high telomerase activity, and is used in a testing platform aimed at detecting cancer cells in the blood. It is building an in-house manufacturing system at Kobe Research Lab in Kobe, Hyogo Prefecture.
entries.63744a67ab0e87bc: It is a genetically modified adenovirus that specifically replicates in cancer cells. It is being developed for solid cancers such as esophageal cancer, and in December 2025 it submitted an application in Japan for manufacturing and marketing approval as a regenerative medicine product for esophageal cancer. In Japan, Fujifilm Toyama Chemical Co., Ltd. is scheduled to sell it, and in Taiwan commercialization rights have been licensed to Medigen Biotechnology Corp. Manufacturing is outsourced to other manufacturing companies.
entries.b0e47a9ea2212856: A virus-based drug discovery biotech venture that develops drug candidates such as oncolytic viruses and aims to generate revenue through licensing income and its own sales.
